title: Achieving Nearly-Optimal Regret and Sample Complexity in Dueling Bandits with Applications in Online Recommendations

problem.claim: Dueling bandits require online preference learning from pairwise comparisons while addressing both regret minimization and best arm identification.

gap.claim: Conventional research treats regret minimization and best arm identification as conflicting objectives.

contributions.claim: A framework reduces best arm identification in dueling bandits to a sequential noisy identification problem.
A black-box reduction transforms any regret minimization algorithm into a best arm identification algorithm.
The reduction with an optimal regret minimization algorithm achieves optimal sample complexity and nearly-optimal cumulative weak regret simultaneously.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper proposes a novel framework demonstrating near-consistency between regret minimization and best arm identification in dueling bandits.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The proposed algorithm achieves nearly-optimal best arm identification sample complexity and order-wise best-known cumulative weak regret simultaneously.
Experiments on synthetic benchmarks and real-world online recommendation tasks are reported to validate the method's effectiveness and support its theoretical findings.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper situates dueling bandits in online preference learning with pairwise comparison feedback and applications including recommendations and LLM alignment.
It distinguishes regret minimization from best arm identification and describes their typical goals.
It identifies the conventional treatment of the two objectives as conflicting.
It introduces a reduction-based framework connecting the objectives and derives theoretical guarantees.
It reports near-optimal algorithmic results and experiments on synthetic and recommendation-task benchmarks.

unknowns: Specific regret minimization algorithm and reduction procedure details are not provided.
Theoretical assumptions, quantitative bounds, experimental configurations, and comparison baselines are not specified.
